title: Loyalty cards
summary: Every store card on your phone: pick the store, scan, show it at the till.
description:
**Loyalty cards** keeps your store cards, membership cards and vouchers on your phone, ready at the till. No account, no ads, and it works without a connection.

### Add a card in two taps
- **Pick the store, scan, done.** The store list shows the popular stores of your country first (Slovakia, Czechia or an international list, chosen from your phone's language) as colourful card-shaped tiles. Tap one and the scanner opens straight away; the card is saved the moment the barcode is read.
- **Scan first** and tap the store after, **search** for a store as you type (accents not needed), or add **any other card** by name.
- **No scanner at hand?** Type the number under the barcode on the number keypad: the barcode type is worked out from it, and a mistyped last digit is caught before you get to the till. Or read it from a screenshot or photo.

### At the till
- Tap a card and its code fills the screen on white, with the number under it in large digits for typing by hand. The screen goes to **full brightness and stays on** while the code shows.
- **Swipe sideways** to the next card without going back.
- Codes are drawn by the app itself: EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, Code 128, Code 39, Code 93, Codabar, ITF, QR code, Data Matrix, PDF417 and Aztec.

### Your wallet
- Every card as a face in its store's colour, or with **your own photo** of the card. Favourites first, then the cards you use most (or last used, or A to Z). Search by store, number, name or note.
- Points or balance, expiry date with a **reminder a week before**, the name on the card, a note, and photos of the front and back.
- Archive cards you no longer use; share a card's code with someone in your family.
- A **home-screen widget** with your favourite cards.

### Bring your cards along
- **From screenshots:** take a screenshot of each card in the app you used before, pick them all at once, and tap the store under each picture. The barcode is read on your phone.
- **From a file:** imports the card list CSV most card wallet apps export (store, card number, barcode type, notes, expiry, points; comma or semicolon), including the card table those apps write into their backups. Cards you already have are left alone.
- **Back up** all your cards to a CSV file, for example for a new phone.

### What it never does
- No ads, no tracking, no analytics, no account and no sign-in.
- It cannot connect to the internet. Nothing leaves your phone unless you share a card or save a backup yourself.
- It holds no payment cards: store and membership cards only. Store names are shown as plain text in the app's own colours; it ships no logos.

In English and Slovak, following your phone's language.

research.used_for: What a leading offline card wallet offers: thousands of store templates, scan or type a card, import several cards at once from screenshots, works offline, backups without an account, no ads.
How people move cards between wallets: a screenshot of each card, all picked at once, one card made from each; scan or type as the other ways in; what reviewers liked (looks, speed) and missed.
A store list with the cards of many European countries as the fast way to add a card; a custom card with your own picture for stores not in it; local storage and transfer by QR code.
What users praise in a simple card wallet: no ads, no sign-in, a clean design.
Simplicity as the reason people pick a card wallet; extras that can make one feel bare.
What reviewers value: most-used or recently used cards at the top, notes and photos, working offline, a code that does not fail at the checkout; complaints about being pushed to create an account.
Adding a loyalty card by tapping or searching the store's or programme's name, then scanning the card or typing its number.
Adding a pass from a photo or screenshot of its barcode; what to do when a till cannot scan a code.
The Slovak card-wallet market: a widely used wallet closing and moving its users to an app with an account, and the card wallets Slovak shoppers turn to instead.
The most known and most used loyalty programmes in Czechia (a supermarket chain's card first, a pharmacy chain's most used), for the Czech store list.
Which cards Czech shoppers carry (supermarkets, drugstores, pharmacies), for the order of the Czech store list.
A common complaint: a code drawn in the wrong barcode type is refused at the till, so a scanned card keeps the type it was scanned in.
Why the code is shown at full brightness: a dim screen is the first reason a phone's code does not scan at the register.
Core functions of an offline card wallet: scan with the camera, type a code when there is no usable barcode, card colours, backup and transfer to a new phone, share a card, import from files.
Barcode types a card wallet is expected to handle (13 symbologies, including Aztec, Codabar, Code 93 and ITF, all offered since 2.1.0), fully offline use, importing from other wallets.

Expected extras: groups, archive, star, balance, expiry and valid-from dates, notes, front and back photos, reading a barcode from an image, brighter screen when showing a code, home-screen shortcuts and widget, CSV import and export, search that ignores accents.
Why the category needs a local-first app: a large card wallet shut down in December 2024 and moved users to an app with an account.

Catima's export: a zip holding catima.csv with several tables (a version line, groups, cards, card groups) separated by blank lines. The cards table has _id, store, note, validfrom, expiry and balance (epoch milliseconds, numbers), balancetype, cardid, barcodeid, barcodetype (enum names such as CODE_128, EAN_13, QR_CODE), barcodeencoding, headercolor, starstatus, lastused, archive. Only that table, saved on its own, can be imported.

The column names of that cards table (store, cardid, barcodeid, barcodetype, expiry, balance, starstatus, archive), mapped onto store, card number, barcode type, valid until, points, pinned and archived.

migration.summary: Imports a card list CSV (store, card number, barcode type; comma or semicolon), the card table card wallet apps put in their backups, and this app's own backup.

samples.about: This app’s own backup: adds 3 cards, one pinned and one archived
A card wallet’s card table: enum barcode types (ITF kept), expiry in milliseconds, star and archive flags: adds 6 cards
Hand-made list: semicolons, Shop and Barcode format columns, dotted dates: adds 5, skips a too-short EAN-13
